name: Circulation of the blood
kb: Harvey's demonstration that blood circulates in a closed loop, driven by the heart
note: Not that blood moves, but that it circulates: same blood returns to the heart, not consumed, and the quantity is small enough that arterial blood must reach veins via capillaries

name: Lung gas exchange
kb: Oxygen enters blood through lungs, carbon dioxide leaves
note: The kernel: lungs do not simply absorb blood like a sponge, they exchange gases across a thin barrier

name: Digestive process
kb: Food is broken down by enzymes into absorbable nutrients
note: Not just mechanical grinding: chemical transformation by acid and ferments, absorption through intestinal wall

name: Nervous system structure and function
kb: Brain, spinal cord and nerves form a communication network
note: Not simple mechanical tubes but specialized tissue conducting electrical signals; distinction between sensory and motor nerves

name: Endocrine glands and hormones
kb: Glands secrete substances that regulate body functions remotely
note: Distinction between nervous (electrical) and endocrine (chemical) signaling; hormones as circulating chemical messengers

name: Kidney filtration
kb: Kidney filters waste from blood while conserving water and salts
note: Not simple sieving; selective reabsorption of useful substances and variable water retention

name: Immune system and antibodies
kb: Body produces specific substances that neutralize pathogens
note: Specific immunity: different pathogens provoke different antibodies; second exposure produces faster response

name: Cell as basic unit of life
kb: All living things composed of cells, each cell from pre-existing cell
note: Not just observation of cells under lens, but the theory that organisation is cellular throughout, not fibrous or humoral

name: Mendelian inheritance laws
kb: Traits inherited as discrete factors in predictable ratios
note: Not blending but discrete particles; dominance and recessiveness; 3:1 and 9:3:3:1 ratios in crosses

name: Chromosome and heredity
kb: Hereditary factors located on chromosomes in nucleus
note: Direct observation: chromosomes visible at meiosis and mitosis; map genes to chromosome locations

name: Gene as unit of inheritance
kb: Discrete heritable unit responsible for single trait or enzyme
note: Gene not mere bead on string but active agent; one gene one enzyme; mutation as change in gene

name: DNA as hereditary material
kb: Deoxyribonucleic acid carries genetic information
note: Double helix structure; base pairing; information stored in sequence; DNA replication fidelity

name: Stethoscope
kb: Acoustic instrument for listening to heart, lungs and viscera
note: Laennec's tube: stiffened paper initially, then wood; acoustic coupling transforms inaudible vibrations to audible without stethoscope being nearly as gross as hands on chest

name: Percussion technique
kb: Tapping body surface to assess underlying organs by resonance
note: Auenbrugger's method: tapping chest produces different notes over fluid, solid, air; requires training to distinguish

name: Systematic auscultation
kb: Listening through stethoscope to recognize normal and abnormal sounds
note: Not just listening but cataloguing: rales, rhonchi, murmurs, clicks; correlation with pathology and prognosis

name: Clinical thermometer
kb: Sealed liquid-in-glass thermometer calibrated for body temperature
note: Standardized range 35-42 C, mercury bulb, constriction trap to keep mercury in place after withdrawal, readable in one minute

name: Sphygmomanometer
kb: Device for measuring blood pressure
note: Riva-Rocci cuff and column: cuff inflated until radial pulse disappears, pressure read from mercury manometer, deflation to systolic and diastolic points

name: Ophthalmoscope
kb: Instrument for direct visualization of retina and optic disc
note: Helmholtz's coaxial light path: light source and observer on same axis; mirror with central hole; correct focus requires interpretation

name: Otoscope
kb: Speculum and magnification for direct ear canal visualization
note: Simple conical speculum plus lens; not just view but teach recognition of cerumen, infection, perforation, light reflex

name: Laryngoscope
kb: Mirror on handle for indirect visualization of larynx
note: Indirect laryngoscopy: angled mirror reflects light and image back; direct intubation for anesthesia came later

name: Rigid endoscope
kb: Straight tube with distal lens for inspecting internal cavities
note: Early versions for urethra and bladder; later gastroscopy; achromatic objective required; light source separate initially, then coaxial

name: Cystoscope
kb: Specialized rigid endoscope for bladder visualization
note: Fenestrated sheath; working channel for instrumentation; direct vision of trigone, ureteral orifices and mucosa

name: X-ray radiography
kb: Radiograph for imaging bones and soft tissues
note: X-ray tube, transformer for high voltage, cooling, filtration for soft rays, photographic plate exposure time; fluoroscopy followed

name: Fluoroscopy imaging
kb: Real-time X-ray imaging on fluorescent screen
note: Barium sulfate fluorescence visible in dark; lead glass shielding; carbon arc or tungsten target; image intensification came much later

name: Contrast media
kb: Radiopaque substances to outline hollow organs and blood vessels
note: Barium swallow for GI tract; urography for urinary system; early iodine compounds for angiography; toxicity and allergic reaction gradually recognized

name: Electrocardiogram
kb: Recording of electrical activity of heart
note: String galvanometer initially; three standard bipolar leads; later six unipolar; PQRST waves; arrhythmias and ischemia visible

name: Electroencephalogram
kb: Recording of electrical activity of brain
note: Scalp electrodes; low voltage millivolt signals require vacuum tube amplification; alpha waves at rest; seizure spikes; sleep stages

name: Basal metabolic rate measurement
kb: Quantification of resting energy expenditure from oxygen consumption
note: Measured during fasting sleep; oxygen consumption or carbon dioxide production; thyroid function assessment; reproducibility requires strict conditions

name: Haemocytometer
kb: Counting chamber for red blood cell enumeration
note: Precisely ruled counting grid; known depth; dilution factor; normal range and interpretation of anemia and polycythemia

name: Differential white cell count
kb: Classification and counting of white blood cell types
note: Blood smear stained and examined under oil immersion; neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, basophils; left shift in infection

name: Urinalysis
kb: Chemical and microscopic examination of urine
note: Specific gravity, pH, protein, glucose, ketones, bilirubin; crystals and casts under microscope; infection indicated by bacteria and white cells

name: Blood glucose measurement
kb: Quantification of glucose in blood serum
note: Fasting baseline; response to glucose load; distinction between diabetes and hypoglycemia; Somogyi effect and brittle diabetes

name: Wassermann test
kb: Complement fixation test for syphilis serology
note: Antibodies in syphilitic serum fix complement; addition of sensitized RBC shows hemolysis or lack thereof; false positives in lupus and atypical pneumonia

name: Tuberculin test
kb: Intradermal injection of tuberculin to detect TB sensitization
note: Mantoux test: intradermal injection of purified protein derivative; delayed hypersensitivity reaction; induration size interpretation; active vs latent TB

name: Tissue biopsy
kb: Sampling of living tissue for pathological examination
note: Needle or punch biopsy; immediate fixation; staining and microscopy; diagnosis of malignancy, inflammation, infection without surgical exploration

name: Frozen section histology
kb: Rapid histological examination during surgery using cryostat
note: Specimen frozen in cryostat at -20 C; thin sections cut without embedding; rapid staining; intraoperative diagnosis for tumor margins and unexpected findings

name: Autoclave sterilizer
kb: Steam sterilization of surgical instruments at pressure
note: Prevost and Junker's pressure vessel; 120 C at 2 atmospheres; spore kill vs vegetative cell; correct loading and cycles critical

name: Surgical glove
kb: Rubber glove barrier for surgeon's hands
note: Halsted's gloves: latex not yet vulcanized properly so degraded; talc powder inside for donning; protective not just of patient but of surgeon

name: Surgical facemask
kb: Gauze mask to reduce respiratory droplet contamination
note: Initially cloth; later gauze in layers; protection of surgical field from oral and nasal flora; not protection of wearer

name: Surgical gown
kb: Sterile gown worn by operating surgeon
note: Initially ordinary cotton; later white linen for visibility of blood; design prevents microbial shedding from body; sleeves fully extended

name: Sterile drape
kb: Sterile fabric to define and maintain operative field
note: Towels and sheets arranged in layers; fenestration to expose only site; edges kept moist to prevent microbial wicking

name: Catgut suture
kb: Absorbable suture from animal intestine
note: Not cat but sheep or horse; prepared from submucosa; caliber standardization; chromic acid treatment for slower absorption

name: Synthetic suture
kb: Non-absorbable synthetic fiber for wound closure
note: Nylon monofilament; less inflammation than catgut; does not dissolve; surgical silk still used for specialized purposes

name: Surgical haemostat
kb: Clamp or forceps for hemostasis during surgery
note: Pean, Kelly, mosquito; teeth and serrated jaws; spring handles; ratchet locking; arterial vs venous clamps

name: Self-retaining retractor
kb: Mechanical retraction of wound edges without assistant
note: Balfour, Weitlaner designs; arms with adjustable blades; ratchet or screw adjustments; frees assistant for other duties

name: Surgical electrocautery
kb: High-frequency electrical current for hemostasis and tissue cutting
note: Monopolar and bipolar designs; cutting current vs coagulation; minimal tissue damage vs spark coagulation; safety protocols for anesthesia

name: Surgical tourniquet
kb: Pneumatic or mechanical device for limb ischemia during surgery
note: Bloodless field enables fine dissection; time limit critical to prevent tissue necrosis; cuff pressure above systolic; Esmarch exsanguination

name: Blood transfusion
kb: Transfer of whole blood or components to recipient
note: Whole blood or separated components; indications for hemorrhage and anemia; citrate anticoagulation; compatibility testing beforehand

name: Blood typing and cross-matching
kb: ABO and Rh blood group determination for transfusion safety
note: Landsteiner's groups; major and minor cross-match; agglutination reactions; hemolytic transfusion reactions from mismatch

name: Blood bank and storage
kb: Organized collection, testing and preservation of blood units
note: Donor screening and testing; refrigeration at 4 C; citrate anticoagulation; shelf life limitations; coordinated supply for emergencies

name: Citrate anticoagulation
kb: Sodium citrate solution to prevent clotting in stored blood
note: Citrate binds calcium needed for coagulation cascade; citrate toxicity from massive transfusion; later use in dialysis

name: Intravenous saline solution
kb: Sterile 0.9% sodium chloride solution for fluid replacement
note: Isotonic with plasma; no hemolysis; replaces losses from hemorrhage and dehydration; colloid vs crystalloid later debated

name: Anaesthetic machine
kb: Device for delivery of anesthetic gases with oxygen
note: Cylinders, regulators, flowmeters, vaporizer, carbon dioxide absorber, reservoir bag, mask and circuit; precise mixing prevents hypoxia

name: Endotracheal intubation
kb: Placement of tube in trachea for controlled ventilation
note: Direct vision with laryngoscope; cuffed tube prevents aspiration; IPPV with mechanical ventilation; complications from prolonged intubation

name: Spinal anaesthesia
kb: Injection of local anesthetic into cerebrospinal fluid
note: Bier and Corning puncture; level of blockade; hypotension and bradycardia; post-dural puncture headache; advantages over general for lower surgeries

name: Local infiltration anaesthesia
kb: Infiltration of local anesthetic into surgical site
note: Initial cocaine; later procaine and lidocaine; epinephrine added for vasoconstriction and prolonged effect; nerve blocks more selective

name: Appendicectomy
kb: Surgical removal of inflamed appendix
note: McBurney's point incision; ligation of appendicular artery; stump inversion; early diagnosis critical to prevent perforation and peritonitis

name: Hernia repair
kb: Surgical closure of abdominal wall defect
note: Identification of defect; dissection of sac; return of viscera; fascial layer closure; recurrence common with simple suture alone

name: Gastrectomy
kb: Partial or total surgical removal of stomach
note: For ulcer or malignancy; Billroth I and II anastomoses; blood supply from left gastric, right gastric and gastroepiploic vessels

name: Caesarean section
kb: Surgical delivery of baby by incision through uterus
note: Lower segment transverse vs classical vertical; classical not repeated in later pregnancies; perimortem indication when vaginal delivery not safe

name: Orthopaedic internal fixation
kb: Metallic devices for fracture stabilization without external cast
note: Plates, screws and wires; compression plating; timing of mobilization; infection and delayed union complications

name: Plaster cast immobilization
kb: Plaster-of-Paris cast for fracture immobilization
note: Calcined gypsum and water; heat of hydration; padding for comfort; split cast to accommodate swelling; window for skin inspection

name: Skeletal traction
kb: Direct pull on bone via pin for fracture reduction and immobilization
note: Pin or wire through bone; pulleys and weights; femoral traction for hip fracture; weeks of bedrest; skin care critical

name: Skin grafting
kb: Transfer of skin from donor to recipient site for wound coverage
note: Full thickness vs split thickness; donor site must heal; vascularization of graft; autograft only option early; allograft rejection

name: Cataract extraction
kb: Surgical removal of opaque lens
note: Intracapsular vs extracapsular; phacoemulsification came much later; post-operative aphakia managed with thick glasses

name: Thyroidectomy
kb: Surgical removal of thyroid gland
note: Iodine preparation to reduce vascularity; recurrent laryngeal nerve identification; hypoparathyroidism from inadvertent gland removal; thyroid storm crisis

name: Digitalis glycosides
kb: Cardiac glycosides from foxglove for heart failure
note: Withering's empirical observation; positive inotropic and negative chronotropic; narrow therapeutic window; digitalis toxicity from accumulation

name: Morphine isolation
kb: Purified alkaloid from opium poppy
note: Serturner's work; crystalline form; injection and oral routes; respiratory depression and addiction risks

name: Quinine isolation
kb: Alkaloid from cinchona bark for malaria
note: Pelletier and Caventou isolation; crystal form; bitter taste led to tonic water; cinchonism from high doses; synthetic substitutes later developed

name: Salicylate and aspirin
kb: Salicylic acid and acetyl-salicylic acid for fever and pain
note: Willow bark traditional; salicin to salicylate to acetylation; Bayer's aspirin; anticoagulant effect discovered later

name: Barbiturate sedatives
kb: Barbituric acid derivatives for sedation and anesthesia
note: Barbital, phenobarbital, pentobarbital; intravenous and oral; dependence and withdrawal; narrow margin between sedation and respiratory depression

name: Insulin extraction
kb: Pancreatic hormone for diabetes mellitus
note: Banting and Best 1921; pancreatic extract; purification; potency standardization in units; subcutaneous injection; insulin shock therapy

name: Thyroid hormone extract
kb: Thyroid tissue or thyroxine for hypothyroidism
note: Desiccated thyroid tissue; later synthetic thyroxine; monitoring with BMR or TSH absent; potency variability

name: Adrenaline isolation
kb: Epinephrine from adrenal medulla for anaphylaxis and shock
note: Takamine 1901 isolation; synthetic by 1906; cardiac and vascular effects; hypertensive crisis; added to local anesthetics for vasoconstriction

name: Sulphonamide drugs
kb: Sulfanilamide and derivatives as bacteriostatic agents
note: Domagk's work; competitive antagonism of para-aminobenzoic acid; Prontosil red dye prodrug; broad spectrum but streptococcal resistance

name: Penicillin cultivation
kb: Mold culture for penicillin production
note: Penicillium notatum on culture plates; broth fermentation; antibiotic activity in filtrate; scaling to deep tank fermentation

name: Deep tank fermentation
kb: Large-scale submerged fermentation for penicillin production
note: Aeration and agitation; temperature and pH control; foaming control with silicone; corn steep liquor as nitrogen source; yield improvement over years

name: Freeze-drying penicillin
kb: Lyophilization for stable penicillin storage and transport
note: Vacuum and low temperature sublimation; water removal; stable powder form; reconstitution before injection; crystal structure preservation

name: Streptomycin isolation
kb: Antibiotic from Streptomyces actinomycete for tuberculosis
note: Waksman's screening; first effective TB drug; ototoxicity and renal damage at high doses; resistance development in monotherapy

name: Antitoxin serum therapy
kb: Specific antibodies raised in animals for passive immunization
note: Horse serum; diphtheria and tetanus antitoxins; immediate but transient protection; serum sickness from foreign protein

name: Smallpox vaccine
kb: Vaccinia virus for active immunity to smallpox
note: Jenner's cowpox observation; lymph from pustule; arm-to-arm transfer; lyophilization for storage; eradication by vaccination

name: Rabies vaccine
kb: Killed rabies virus for post-exposure prophylaxis
note: Pasteur's nerve tissue vaccine; duck egg culture later; post-bite series; timing critical before symptom onset

name: Typhoid vaccine
kb: Killed Salmonella typhi for typhoid fever prevention
note: Heat-killed or chemical inactivation; partial protection; revaccination needed; enteric fever still endemic in poor sanitation

name: Cholera vaccine
kb: Vibrio cholerae inactivated vaccine
note: Killed phenol-treated organisms; mucosal immunity weak with injected vaccine; oral rehydration more life-saving than vaccination

name: Plague vaccine
kb: Yersinia pestis inactivated vaccine
note: Killed bacillus; variable efficacy; antiplague serum more immediately useful; vector control reduces need for vaccination

name: Diphtheria toxoid
kb: Detoxified diphtheria toxin for active immunization
note: Formalin-detoxified toxin retains immunogenicity; more effective than killed organism; Schick test for immunity status

name: Tetanus toxoid
kb: Detoxified tetanus toxin for active immunization
note: Formalin inactivation of toxin; effective but slower than antitoxin; booster doses maintain immunity; wound prophylaxis combination with antitoxin

name: Pertussis vaccine
kb: Killed Bordetella pertussis for whooping cough prevention
note: Whole cell killed vaccine; high fever and local reaction; acellular vaccine much later; maternal antibodies in infant protection

name: Yellow fever vaccine
kb: Live attenuated yellow fever virus for immunization
note: 17D strain attenuation; long-lived immunity; dengue and other flaviviruses cross-protect partially; vector control still needed

name: Vitamin A and deficiency
kb: Fat-soluble vitamin for vision and epithelial health
note: Night blindness and xerophthalmia from deficiency; provitamin A in beta-carotene; hypervitaminosis A toxicity; fortification of milk

name: Vitamin B1 thiamine
kb: Thiamine for energy metabolism
note: Beriberi from deficiency; rice bran source; wet vs dry beriberi; Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome in alcoholism

name: Vitamin B12 cobalamin
kb: Cobalt-containing vitamin for DNA synthesis and nerve function
note: Pernicious anemia from intrinsic factor deficiency; injected when oral absorption fails; only animal source; methylmalonuria in deficiency

name: Vitamin C ascorbic acid
kb: Water-soluble vitamin for collagen synthesis and immunity
note: Scurvy from deficiency; citrus and fresh fruit source; wound healing impaired; role in infection and immunity

name: Vitamin D cholecalciferol
kb: Fat-soluble vitamin for calcium absorption
note: Rickets from deficiency; cod liver oil source; sun exposure activation; secondary hyperparathyroidism in deficiency

name: Iodised salt
kb: Salt with added potassium iodide for goiter prevention
note: Endemic goiter in iodine-poor regions; iodine content degrades with time; fortification acceptance varies culturally

name: Oral rehydration solution
kb: Glucose-electrolyte solution for diarrheal disease rehydration
note: WHO/UNICEF ORS; glucose-sodium cotransport in small intestine; as effective as IV therapy; salt ratio critical

name: Sand filtration
kb: Slow sand filters for water purification
note: Biofilm layer (schmutzdecke) removes particles and pathogens; slow rate; microorganism breakthrough possible; pre-treatment needed

name: Water chlorination
kb: Chlorine disinfection of water
note: Free and combined chlorine; residual for distribution; trihalomethane formation from organic matter; hypochlorite solution easier than gas

name: Separate sewage collection
kb: Separation of storm water and sanitary sewage
note: Storm overflows during rain; prevents plant overload; but combined systems cheaper; infiltration and inflow challenges

name: Activated sludge treatment
kb: Biological sewage treatment with aeration and microorganisms
note: Microorganism flocs oxidize organic matter; aeration essential; solids separation by settling; sludge recycling; process control critical

name: Milk pasteurisation
kb: Heat treatment of milk to kill pathogens
note: Low-temperature long-time or high-temperature short-time; kills TB, brucella, campylobacter; spoilage organisms also reduced

name: Meat inspection
kb: Systematic inspection of slaughtered animals for disease
note: Visual and palpation; tuberculosis, anthrax, trichinosis detection; condemned meat; documentation of inspection

name: Food purity legislation
kb: Legal standards for food composition and safety
note: Definition of adulterant; food standards; labeling requirements; enforcement and penalties; detection of substitutes

name: Notifiable disease system
kb: Legal requirement to report certain infectious diseases
note: Surveillance for outbreaks; data collection; confidentiality protection; rapid reporting for emerging threats

name: Contact tracing
kb: Identification and monitoring of disease contacts
note: Case finding and source identification; quarantine placement; cohort management; resource-intensive but effective for containment

name: Isolation hospital
kb: Dedicated facility for infectious disease isolation
note: Site isolation and water supply; large grounds for convalescence; design for natural ventilation; segregation by disease

name: Vector control
kb: Elimination or reduction of disease-transmitting insects
note: Mosquito, flea, louse identification; breeding site destruction; chemical insecticides; resistance development

name: Mosquito bed net
kb: Mesh net for protection against mosquitoes
note: Simple barrier; treated with insecticide for duration; major malaria control tool; high coverage critical for population effect

name: Improved pit latrine
kb: Designed excrement pit with flyproof superstructure
note: Containment of fecal matter; prevention of contamination of water and food; ventilation for odor and fly prevention

name: Hospital infection control
kb: Systematic measures to prevent nosocomial infection
note: Hand hygiene; environmental cleaning; isolation precautions; sterilization of equipment; staff education and compliance

name: Maternal health clinic
kb: Scheduled antenatal and postnatal health services for women
note: Screening for hypertension and proteinuria; dietary advice; postpartum hemorrhage and infection prevention; early detection of problems

name: Child health clinic
kb: Scheduled immunization and development monitoring for children
note: Vaccination records; growth monitoring; disease surveillance; screening for developmental delay; accident prevention counseling

name: Case record keeping
kb: Systematic written record of patient history, examination and treatment
note: Standardized form and order; problem list; assessment and plan; longitudinal follow-up; quality of care measure

name: Case series analysis
kb: Descriptive collection and analysis of similar cases
note: Pattern recognition; natural history description; hypothesis generation; no control group; rapid publication possible

name: Cohort study
kb: Follow exposed and unexposed groups forward in time
note: Prospective or retrospective; relative risk calculation; attrition and confounding challenges; expensive but strong evidence

name: Case-control study
kb: Compare exposure history in cases and controls
note: Odds ratio approximates relative risk; efficient for rare diseases; recall bias and selection bias risks; faster than cohort

name: Randomised controlled trial
kb: Randomized allocation of treatment and control with defined outcome measures
note: Gold standard for efficacy evidence; eliminates selection bias; requires large sample sizes; protocol registration and monitoring critical

name: Blinding in trials
kb: Concealment of treatment assignment to prevent bias
note: Single blind subject only, double blind subject and investigator, triple blind adds assessor; unblinding for safety; masked capsules and injections

name: Placebo control
kb: Inert treatment given to control group to assess true effect vs expectation
note: Ethical constraints: cannot use placebo when proven treatment exists; placebo effect real but separate from pharmacological effect

name: Medical statistics
kb: Statistical methods applied to medical data
note: Hypothesis testing; confidence intervals; power calculations; multiple comparison corrections; software automation

name: Mortality table
kb: Actuarial analysis of age-specific mortality for population
note: Life expectancy calculation; actuarial science; insurance basis; improved sanitation and childhood survival change tables markedly

name: Vital registration system
kb: Official recording of births and deaths with cause
note: Legal proof of identity; cause of death requires physician; population denominator for rates; undercount in poor regions

name: Professional nursing
kb: Trained nursing staff for patient care
note: Nightingale training standards; apprenticeship in hospital; gender issues in recruitment; autonomy vs physician delegation

name: Cadaver dissection
kb: Systematic anatomical dissection of human corpses for education
note: Legal cadaver supply from executed criminals and unclaimed poor; religious objections; reveals anatomy without speculation

name: Medical licensing
kb: Examination and licensing requirement to practice medicine
note: Qualification standards; examination by peers; legal monopoly; disciplinary power; excludes charlatans but also innovation

name: Medical journal publication
kb: Peer-reviewed periodic publication of medical research
note: Priority claims and knowledge dissemination; peer review for quality; citation tracking; reproducibility and fraud detection

name: Pharmacopoeia
kb: Official compendium of drugs with standards for preparation and purity
note: Prescription reference; legal authority; assurance of composition and quality; updated as new drugs appear and old ones refined

name: Drug standardisation
kb: Biological assays to establish potency standards for drugs
note: Units of activity for biologics like insulin and antitoxin; animal testing for potency; variation in natural products

name: Bioassay
kb: Biological measurement of substance potency
note: In vivo measurement; reproducibility; refinement with statistical design; reduces animal use compared to crude testing

name: Methylene blue staining
kb: Methylene blue dye for visualizing blood cells and microorganisms
note: Gram and acid-fast stain modifications; vivid blue color; bacteria and WBC visible; Ehrlich's discovery

name: Spirometer
kb: Instrument to measure lung volumes and flow rates
note: Dry or water-sealed bell; volume displaced; obstructive vs restrictive pattern recognition

name: Surgical light source
kb: Bright light for surgical illumination
note: Carbon arc initially; tungsten filament later; reflector geometry; color temperature; heat dissipation

name: Microbiology culture technique
kb: Growth of microorganisms on culture media for identification
note: Petri dishes with agar; colony morphology; Gram stain; culture identification; antibiotic sensitivity testing

name: Plant chemistry extraction
kb: Extraction and isolation of active compounds from plants
note: Solvent selection; concentration; crystallization; identity verification; standardization of final product

name: Agar culture media
kb: Standardized growth medium for microbiology culture
note: Peptone, beef extract and agar; selective and differential media; pouring and storage; shelf-life management
